claims.statement: TVI-CAMS is an internal multi-tenant compliance working layer for TVI schools running TESDA scholarship batches (TWSP/CFSP); TESDA SIS/T2MIS/BSRS remain the authoritative systems and UI copy must never imply official approval or submission (RULES rule 27).

The app is Next.js 16 App Router (next ^16.4.3, dev runs next dev --webpack), React 19.2.4, strict TypeScript, Tailwind v4, Clerk (@clerk/nextjs ^7.4.1 with ClerkProvider in the root layout), and pnpm (packageManager pnpm@9.15.4).
Node 22+ is hard-required: Vitest 4's rolldown calls util.styleText with an array argument that throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE on Node 21 or older, before any test loads.

The app talks directly to one hosted Supabase project (Postgres + Storage) with no separate backend and no staging environment; Express.js (Node/TypeScript) is documented as a future-only backend direction that must not be built or treated as present.

proxy.ts (repo root) is the Clerk middleware whose matcher covers every non-static route plus __clerk and api/trpc; it stamps an x-pathname header for Server Components and does not itself force authentication.

Route protection is enforced per protected surface, not by proxy.ts: app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx calls requireAuthenticatedUser() from modules/auth/data/auth.ts and redirects anonymous visitors to /sign-in, app/page.tsx is a bare 307 redirect to /dashboard, /api/openapi.json checks getAuthUserId() itself and answers 401, and the Clerk webhook is unauthenticated by design because it verifies Clerk's request signature instead.

The dashboard layout resolves identity once before rendering and feeds every downstream decision from it: one getProfileSnapshot read supplies role, name and tenant list, resolveTrustedRole narrows the role (falling back to null, which callers narrow to viewer), and isPlatformAdmin is a separate ADR-006 axis read over a security definer RPC because public.platform_admins is unreadable through the anon client. A failed platform-admin check hides the nav row instead of rendering a link into a denial.

The server-side Supabase client is built with the anon key and an accessToken callback that returns the Clerk session token; a missing token throws NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE rather than silently querying as anon, because RLS against anon returns zero rows with no error — the dangerous outcome for a compliance tool. The throw is lazy: it fires inside the callback when the query runs, not at client construction, so callers see it as a query error and map it to sync-failed; the exported sentinel lets the dev-only /api/debug/auth-check route separate 'not signed in' from 'token rejected', and that route returns 404 in production.

Postgres RLS (app_private.* helper functions from the canonical migration, reading only sub from the JWT) makes every authorization decision — RLS is the security boundary and UI hiding is usability only (RULES rule 1); the app uses Clerk's native third-party auth integration because Supabase JWT templates were deprecated 1 Apr 2025 and the schema needs no custom claims.

The service-role client (lib/supabase/service.ts) bypasses RLS and is confined to the Clerk webhook provisioning path — modules/auth/data/provisioning.ts, invoked only from app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts (creates profiles on user.created, deactivates on user.deleted) — and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must never be NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed or read outside that file.
Import direction app → modules → shared → lib/supabase is lint-enforced by import/no-restricted-paths zones in eslint.config.mjs (RULES rule 7, [lint]).

lib/supabase/database.types.ts (generated raw DB row types) may be imported only from module data/ layers and lib/supabase itself — not from app/, shared/, or any module domain/ or ui/ code; components import domain types from shared/types.ts only (RULES rule 10, [lint]).

ESLint zones forbid shared/ from importing modules/ or app/, forbid modules/ from importing app/, and make each of the 14 modules' data/ private to itself (zones generated from the domains array) while app/ may fetch from any module's data/ (RULES rules 8-9, [lint]).

modules/ holds exactly 14 domain modules — one per PRD FR (auth FR-01 through reports FR-15) plus shell for app chrome — the same set named in the ESLint domains array; verified against the tree, seven have a data/ layer (activity, auth, batches, billing, documents, import-export, tenancy), three are README-only (attendance, lamr, notifications), and the remaining four (analytics, reports, settings, shell) have domain/ and/or ui/ code only. New code goes inside its owning module, never in a new top-level folder (RULES rule 12).

modules/tenancy has data/, domain/ and ui/: profile/membership reads and tenant-access folding, user administration, and the ADR-006 school registry, with modules/tenancy/ui/CreateUserForm.tsx and modules/tenancy/ui/CreateSchoolForm.tsx as its public UI surfaces.

Platform admin (ADR-006) is a separate axis from profile_role — resolved via a security definer RPC (isPlatformAdmin in modules/tenancy/data/platform.ts) because public.platform_admins is deliberately unreadable through the anon client — and its reach is the school registry only; granting it any compliance table or letting it seat itself into a tenant is a boundary change needing its own ADR (RULES rule 30).

modules/attendance/, modules/lamr/, and modules/notifications/ are README-only stubs with no code: attendance plans data/attendance.ts + domain/eligibility.ts (ADR-007's dropout rule) against the planned attendance_records table, lamr plans LAMR report fetch/map and evidence UI, and notifications remains unimplemented while alerts are computed on read (the dashboard AlertsPanel still lives in modules/batches/ui/dashboard/).

Where RULES.md and CLAUDE.md appear to disagree, RULES.md wins and the drift should be fixed; below the rules, docs precedence is docs/MASTER_PRD_SRS.md → docs/TRD.md → docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, with the ADRs in docs/adr/ overriding or amending those documents (RULES rules 30-31).

docs/adr/ holds six accepted ADRs that override or amend docs/MASTER_PRD_SRS.md and docs/TRD.md (RULES rules 30-31): ADR-001 (billing is a document-generating engine, superseding 'billing = preparation signal only' wording), ADR-002 (the design prototype portrays the ADR-001 target with no planned-vs-implemented badges, honesty carried by copy), ADR-003 (amends ADR-001 §4: the packet queue is a projection of (batch, billing_type, tranche) with the draft → ready → generated → submitted → settled lifecycle, derived due dates, and user-asserted submitted/settled marks), ADR-004 (a requirement with no record is untracked — a third state excluded from measurement and failing closed at gates, decided in one module), ADR-005 (one tenant membership per profile, a viewer-scoped demo account, and a dev membership seed rather than a migration), and ADR-006 (supersedes PRD FR-02's 'Super Admin is not implemented' with a platform admin that provisions the school registry only).
RULES rule 34 ('no test runner yet — pnpm test is a placeholder') is known drift predating the Vitest stand-up: pnpm test now runs vitest run with 22 unit spec files in tests/unit/.

assets/, preview/, screenshots/, ui_kits/, and uploads/ are ported verbatim from the design bundle: excluded from lint via globalIgnores in eslint.config.mjs, and edit-blocked by the PreToolUse hook .claude/hooks/protect-static-dirs.sh (RULES rule 28, [hook]) which explicitly carves out public/assets/ (the app's real runtime static directory); FIGMA FILES/, diagrams/, and .design-sync/ are review-level design artifacts, not app code (RULES rule 29).

pnpm dev runs next dev --webpack, pnpm build/start build and serve, pnpm lint runs the flat ESLint config, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit strict-typechecks (no dedicated script), pnpm test runs Vitest, pnpm test:e2e runs Playwright with a pnpm-dev web server on :3000, and pnpm preview serves the static design bundle on :5000.

Unit tests cover mappers and pure module domain/ layers with fixed as-of dates; the Playwright spec exercises unauthenticated access to a dashboard route being redirected to /sign-in (the layout gate, not proxy.ts); real-Supabase RLS/tenant-isolation integration tests are still outstanding and must run against the real hosted project with no mocks (RULES rule 35).

supabase/migrations/ holds nine .sql files: 20260528160300_create_tenant_scoped_schema.sql is the canonical first migration for schema + RLS, and 20261024110000_add_dashboard_operational_fields.sql (ADR-008's billing_deadline) is the newest checked in and unapplied. New migrations are additive (RULES rule 20) and dev seed data lives in supabase/seeds/, not migrations/.

proxy.ts is clerkMiddleware with a matcher covering every route except static assets plus __clerk and api/trpc; its only work is stamping x-pathname so Server Components can read the full request path, and it performs no session check and no redirect. Route protection is therefore per protected surface, and app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx's requireAuthenticatedUser() is the only authentication gate.

lib/supabase/server.ts builds an anon-key Supabase client whose accessToken callback returns the Clerk session token (Clerk's native third-party-auth integration, since RLS reads only sub from auth.jwt()). A missing token throws NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE lazily inside the callback rather than returning null, so the query fails and each caller's catch maps it to sync-failed instead of silently reading as anon and returning zero rows.

isSupabaseConfigured() gates client construction in the data layer, so a run without Supabase env vars yields unconfigured snapshots instead of a throw; neither unconfigured nor sync-failed may substitute mock data, and sync-failed must additionally surface the sync-failed banner (RULES rule 19).

/api/openapi.json checks getAuthUserId() itself and answers 401, and POST /api/webhooks/clerk is unauthenticated by design, verifying Clerk's signature via verifyWebhook instead because no session exists to scope it.

The service-role client is confined to one path: lib/supabase/service.ts (which bypasses RLS) is used only by modules/auth/data/provisioning.ts through the Clerk webhook route, which creates profiles on user.created/user.updated and flips is_active = false on user.deleted rather<|place_holder_mm_span_0442|> hard-deleting. SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must never be NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed or read outside that file.

Tenant context is the URL path segment /t/<school>/<section>, a selection over rows RLS already allows rather than an authorization of its own. resolveRouteScope (cache-wrapped) returns a four-way union — ok, no-tenant-access, unknown, not-a-member with a fallback scope — and the t/[tenantCode]/layout.tsx renders each non-ok arm as an honest EmptyState/NoTenantAccessState; a foreign or unknown code never falls back to all schools.

Pages under /t/[tenantCode] call requireScope(), which returns the validated scope or null (the layout already owns the state); it deliberately does not call notFound() because layout and page render in parallel and a thrown 404 could race the layout's friendlier arm. Security does not rest on it either way — without a scope there is no tenant id to query with (RULES rule 2).

Legacy unscoped paths (/batch-cards, /documents, /report, and /dashboard for callers with no trainer/admin redirect) still exist as thin stubs built by legacyRoute() and forward to the same section of the caller's default school through redirectToDefaultScope, preserving search params; only a caller with no school gets NoTenantAccessState, or a couldn't-verify state when the profile read failed.

app/(dashboard)/tenant-access.ts answers the orthogonal is-this-person-in-any-school question by joining modules/auth identity to modules/tenancy's profile read, a join only app/ may make because another module's data/ is private (RULES rule 8); screens then fold its verdict over a snapshot with withTenantAccess, which replaces only an ok snapshot so a real failure is never masked.

MetricsRow lives under the segment it describes — t/[tenantCode]/(sections)/layout.tsx and trainer/layout.tsx — not the root layout, because App Router does not re-render a parent layout on client navigation and a root-owned row kept showing the previous school's numbers after a switch. It is omitted entirely on a non-ok snapshot rather than rendered as zeros.

Role authority is profiles.role via resolveTrustedRole; Clerk is identity only. resolveRouteRole is the presentation variant that honours a ?role= query override, so gating a redirect on it would let a real trainer request ?role=admin and skip it — billing and report redirect trainers on resolveTrustedRole before resolving the display variant.

Admin and coordinator are paired in every policy, so the difference records who someone is, not what they may do. Payload trimming is server-side rather than CSS (RULES rule 5): MetricsRow takes hideBilling, billing/report refuse trainers outright, and viewer is read-only and server-denied on writes (rule 4); Server Actions re-derive the role server-side so a rendered form is never the authority.

Import direction app → modules → shared → lib/supabase is enforced at lint time by import/no-restricted-paths in eslint.config.mjs: database.types.ts is importable only from data/ layers and lib/supabase itself, shared/ may not import modules/ or app/, modules/ may not import app/, and each of the 14 domains gets a generated zone making its data/** private to every other module (RULES rules 7–10).
RULES.md outranks CLAUDE.md wherever the two appear to disagree, and the drift is to be fixed; rule 34 is such a drift, still claiming no test runner exists while tests/unit/ is substantial.

Below RULES.md, docs precedence is docs/MASTER_PRD_SRS.md → docs/TRD.md → docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, all overridden by the ADR chain in docs/adr/ (RULES rule 31), which must be consulted before changing schema or billing math (rule 30).

ADR-007 amended ADR-001 §2 and replaced the fixed ≥5-absence rule with dropout on absences exceeding 20% of the batch's total_sessions or on 3 consecutive unexcused absences, superseding the earlier wording in CONTEXT.md and RULES.md; modules/attendance/README.md now cites the ADR-007 dropout rule.

ADR-008 is proposed and unapplied: it adds a nullable, recorded batches.billing_deadline (already carried by hand in database.types.ts ahead of the migration) so urgency stops counting down from end_date; null means not recorded, never no deadline, and packet due_date stays derived.

pnpm test runs Vitest over tests/unit/, which is substantial and green is the merge gate (mappers and domain rules with fixed as-of dates). The single Playwright spec proves unauthenticated access to /dashboard is redirected to /sign-in by the layout, not proxy.ts. Real-Supabase RLS/tenant-isolation tests are still outstanding and must run against the hosted project with no mocks (RULES rule 35).
